header.act: ACT II — THE COUNCILS TAKE POWER
player.speaker: Revolutionary Delegate
line.reaction-briliant.speaker: Marta Reimers
line.reaction-briliant.text: The yards heard about Kiel before your train arrived. Men who weren't there are telling the story as if they were. Let them talk for now; the garrison is listening.
line.reaction-tactical.speaker: Marta Reimers
line.reaction-tactical.text: The officers have barred the armouries. They read the Kiel casualty telegrams and decided we could be stopped. The yard men still came to meet you, but they'll want to know what happened.
line.reaction-victory.speaker: Marta Reimers
line.reaction-victory.text: They know Kiel is holding. You'll get a hearing in this room. The officers still have the harbour batteries, though; don't let the welcome fool you about that.
line.callback-naval-base.speaker: Bernhard Kuhnt
line.callback-naval-base.text: Because your column held the Kiel naval base, its crews have been sending us everything they can spare. Half the rifles against this wall came north on their wagons.
line.callback-naval-base-lost.speaker: Bernhard Kuhnt
line.callback-naval-base-lost.text: The officers are getting the Kiel base back. We can't count on its magazines. Those rifles may be issued to troops coming after us.
line.callback-comms.speaker: Bernhard Kuhnt
line.callback-comms.text: Our telegraph operators got word of Wilhelmshaven before the Admiralty did. They kept your train moving past the signals the officers tried to close. I'll introduce you when they're off duty.
line.callback-prisoners-freed.speaker: Marta Reimers
line.callback-prisoners-freed.text: The men from the Arrestlokal arrived on the next train. They've been telling everyone about your column at the gate. Some of the sailors here came because of them.
line.callback-prisoners-breakout-partial: The men you pulled through the service gate came north with us. The rest remained behind Souchon's wall. Artelt says the governor may release them; he no longer builds plans on the governor's mercy.
line.callback-prisoners-abandoned.text: The crowd went to the Arrestlokal without us. Steinhäuser's men fired: eight dead, twenty-nine carried away, the cells still locked. I told the families in the telegraph room. The wire worked perfectly, Delegate.
line.parkhaus-scene.speaker: Marta Reimers
line.parkhaus-scene.text: Mind those rifles by the door. There isn't a chair left in the Parkhaus. The telephone operators are bringing the admiral's orders to us before passing them on. Someone has to stay here and answer them.
line.kuhnt-opening.speaker: Bernhard Kuhnt
line.kuhnt-opening.text: These ballots elected the Council of 21. We control the gates and telephone exchange, but the admiral is still issuing orders. I need the council's name on whatever you send out, Delegate.
line.hug-question.speaker: Paul Hug
line.hug-question.text: Aurich, Emden and Oldenburg are waiting to hear from us. Do we send the columns out now? The harbour officers haven't acted yet. They might, once they see how many men have left.
line.hug-question.choice.regional-column: Send columns to Aurich, Emden and Oldenburg. Take delegates who can speak to the workers and garrisons there.
Gain an untested soldiers' detachment and a prestige award, but forgo full core resupply and the entrenched infantry detachment.
line.hug-question.choice.secure-base.tex: Secure the harbour, station, post and armouries. I won't scatter the columns while the officers can take the base back.
line.hug-question.choice.secure-base.hin: Fully resupply every core formation and gain an entrenched infantry detachment, but forgo the soldiers' detachment and prestige award.
line.kuhnt-regional.speaker: Bernhard Kuhnt
line.kuhnt-regional.text: I'll find the delegates. Each column takes someone authorised to help organise a council. Tell the commanders that arriving with rifles doesn't make them the town's government.
line.hug-regional-objection.speaker: Paul Hug
line.hug-regional-objection.text: I will carry the order. But leave me enough men to answer an attack from Oldenburg while the columns are out. A welcome in the towns won't help us hold these gates.
line.hug-consolidate.speaker: Paul Hug
line.hug-consolidate.text: Then make the base secure quickly. The Oldenburg garrison is the greatest remaining obstacle, and delay gives its officers time to isolate the coast.
line.kuhnt-consolidate-objection.speaker: Bernhard Kuhnt
line.kuhnt-consolidate-objection.text: Make it quick. Workers beyond the harbour have already risen because Kiel did. I need to tell them when our columns are coming, not just that we're guarding the stores.
line.oldenburg-report.speaker: Marta Reimers
line.oldenburg-report.text: Every station asks whose orders you carry. Give me copies of the council resolution. I can get railwaymen to stop trains, but they won't do it on my word alone.
line.kuhnt-final.speaker: Bernhard Kuhnt
line.kuhnt-final.text: Take the copies, Marta. The columns leave delegates in each town and disarm officers who organise resistance. If local soldiers join us, let them elect their own representatives. Send their names back here.
